clue.text: I get slab prepared outside fish market

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, wrapped around the fish
the letters of I GET SLAB are prepared, worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone getting a slab of fish ready outside a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' turns I GET SLAB into BILSGATE, and 'outside' wraps it around LING. The answer is London's famous wholesale fish market, so 'fish market' looks like the whole definition, but 'fish' is the LING.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic London wholesale trading place for fish on the Thames, a well-known British example of a market.

clue.text: More masculine although he minces!

definitions.meaning: butch means tough and manly, so this is its comparative form
a man who minces meat in a shop, a meat trader

explanation.surface: A man who is more macho, even though he walks with a mincing gait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minces' suggests an effeminate walk, contrasting with 'masculine'; in fact it is the work of a meat seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of butch, meaning tougher and more manly; also the trade name of someone who prepares and chops meat.

clue.text: Nod head following Shakesperean character study

indicators.note: the letter from Nod comes after the character in the answer

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from Nod

explanation.surface: A drama student nods off while studying a Shakespeare role.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject is to acquire knowledge of it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Kind of tense and not all there

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense describing ongoing past action, as in 'I was walking'

explanation.definitionFit: A grammar term for a past continuous verb form; also means flawed or incomplete, with something missing.

clue.text: Go north of the border

parts.note: looks like an instruction to travel to Scotland, but asks for the Scots word for the verb go, as used north of the English border

explanation.definitionFit: The Scots dialect verb meaning to go or walk, used in Scotland, which lies north of the border with England.

clue.text: Sheer slapper embracing hunk, head over heels

indicators.note: the loose woman holds the other piece inside her, as in an embrace

parts.note: a slapper is British slang for a promiscuous woman, as is goer

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the word for hunk is read backwards

parts.note: a hunk or lump of something is a mass

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman falls head over heels for a hunk, sheer passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' turns MASS into SSAM, which 'embracing' puts inside GOER. 'hunk' suggests a handsome man but is just a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer fabric is extremely fine and transparent, which is what sheer means when describing cloth.

clue.text: Lukewarm's food returned around start of 'Porridge'

indicators.note: the reversed food word goes around the single letter from Porridge
sent back, so the word for food is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: diet means the food a person habitually eats

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner sends back porridge because it is only lukewarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DIET into TEID, which goes 'around' P; the 's after Lukewarm is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid water or food is only slightly warm, the same as lukewarm, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Georgia's beginning to open border for petrol

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia, with the possessive S

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a border is a dividing line

explanation.surface: Georgia opens up its border to imports of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for motor fuel, called petrol in Britain.

clue.text: Do down

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
soft fluffy material, like a sheep's woolly coat

explanation.definitionFit: Means to swindle or cheat someone out of money; as a noun it is a fluffy wool coat, soft like down.

clue.text: Clothes stoutly made, top to toe

indicators.note: the top letter is moved down to the toe, the far end

parts.note: strapping describes someone big, strong and sturdily built

explanation.surface: Clothes for a sturdy person, fitted from head to foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to toe' takes the S from the start of STRAPPING and moves it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are ornamental dress or outward accessories, so the word can mean clothes or finery.

clue.text: Jewel with tip of ruby set in ring

indicators.note: placed inside, as a stone is set in a mount

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A jewel set in a ring alongside a ruby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery but is the sound of bells; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrous gem formed inside an oyster, a classic example of a jewel.

clue.text: Voracious Attila facing Goths, readily yielding initially

parts.note: Attila was a famous leader of the Huns

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Ravenous Attila takes on the Goths, who surrender easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting food intensely, so voracious, a close adjective synonym.

clue.text: Hard compiler, plus, as admitted, fair

indicators.note: let in, so the two words go inside the outer pair

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the setter, the compiler of the crossword, refers to himself as me
and means plus
so can mean as, as in 'so long as'

explanation.surface: A tough crossword setter admits that he is good-looking as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts AND SO inside H and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the old sense of good-looking or attractive, a synonym for a pleasing appearance.

clue.text: Shouted with pride?

parts.note: seems to describe someone yelling proudly, but a pride is a group of lions, so this is the noise lions make

explanation.definitionFit: Lions in a pride make a loud deep cry, the sound that a shouting lion makes.

clue.text: A brisk single's swallowed providing drink

indicators.note: the single letter is taken inside the word for brisk

parts.note: pert means lively and brisk
one, the Roman numeral I, with the 's meaning 'is'
if means providing or on condition that

explanation.surface: A quick single is downed, giving a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Get eating endless dish, scoffing

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the inner piece, as if eating it

parts.note: to derive is to obtain or get something from a source

indicators.note: the word dish with its end letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a dish, gobbling it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips DISH to IS, which 'eating' puts inside DERIVE. 'scoffing' looks like eating greedily but means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing in the sense of jeering or mocking is the same as being contemptuously mocking.

clue.text: Objective is Independent peacekeeper's leader in army

indicators.note: the leader's letter goes inside the word for army

parts.note: martial means relating to the army or war

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An independent peacekeeping chief in the army is fair-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'army' is used as an adjective here, military, giving MARTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Objective means not influenced by personal feelings, which is the meaning of unbiased and fair.

clue.text: Bond chap beat up around introduction to novel

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the letter from novel
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chap is beaten up round about the start of a novel about Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAN into NAT, which goes 'around' N. 'Bond' suggests 007 but means an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal binding agreement or pledge, so a bond in the legal sense.

clue.text: Genesis, Collins' opening helping to keep energy

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the helping holds the energy letter inside it

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Phil Collins opens with music helping keep Genesis energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil Collins was in the rock band Genesis, which the surface plays on; here Genesis is the biblical book of beginnings. 'helping' gives RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means the origin or making of something, as in the making of the world.

clue.text: Copper on trial having highest appeal

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A police officer on trial who is very charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal; 'on' is a link, the first piece written above the second in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of cute, meaning most attractive or appealing.

clue.text: Sort of betting odds on display

definitions.meaning: in sports betting, the range a bookmaker gives for the outcome
an arrangement of things laid out, as a feast or a magazine page

explanation.surface: Odds for one type of betting are set out for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers quote a range for a result in this form of betting; it also means a lavish layout or display.

clue.text: Lady's dead posh and game

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
U means upper-class, the posh classification of language and behaviour
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A deceased upper-class lady who was game for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Lady is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a duke, a noblewoman who holds a title and is addressed as a lady.

clue.text: Headgear for one leg before in tests

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for tests

parts.note: to try is to test, so tries are tests
I is the Roman numeral for one
LB, short for leg before as in lbw, the cricket dismissal

explanation.surface: A batsman wears a hat when given out leg before in Test matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. Leg before is short for leg before wicket, a way of being out in cricket; Tests are international cricket matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft felt hats with a narrow brim, a type of headgear.

clue.text: Set from tenor penned by composer

indicators.note: written inside, enclosed by the composer's name

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach was a composer
T is an abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A selection of tenor parts written by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group or set of things produced or dealt with together.

clue.text: Film doesn't end without right old caper

indicators.note: used in the sense of outside, so the shortened film word goes around the others
the film word loses its last letter

parts.note: a flick is informal for a film

explanation.surface: A movie with an unfinished ending, without its proper old-fashioned caper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't end' turns FLICK into FLIC; 'without' means outside here, so FLIC goes round R and O. 'caper' looks like a heist film but is a playful leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skip or prank, the same as a lively frisky romp.

clue.text: Red head's heart flipping in sheets

indicators.note: only the central letters of the leader's name are turned round

parts.note: Lenin was head of the Reds, the Russian Bolsheviks

explanation.surface: A redhead's heart flutters in bed sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart flipping' turns ENI in the middle of LENIN to INE. 'Red head' suggests a ginger-haired person; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed sheets are made of or are known as household fabric, so the word stands for sheets.

clue.text: Head off decline seen in church

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lapse is a decline or falling off in standards

explanation.surface: Heading off a fall in attendance at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' suggests preventing something but removes the first letter of LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church, a feature found in churches.

clue.text: Broke heart of one in turn

indicators.note: the middle letter goes inside the word for turn

parts.note: a turn is a short comedy act, a skit

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone is broken-hearted at a turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money. 'turn' is a music-hall act.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for having no money at all, penniless.

clue.text: Contrivance very quietly replacing Liberal in Coalition

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out for the other piece

parts.note: an alliance is a coalition
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, a UK political party
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A Liberal quietly replaced in the Coalition government, a political contrivance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the UK Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition of 2010. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or contraption, a mechanical contrivance.

clue.text: Holds on catching batsman, showing guts

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the inner one

parts.note: clings means holds on tightly
a hitter is one who hits, such as a batsman

explanation.surface: A fielder holds on to a catch, getting the batsman out, showing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' suggests courage but means intestines; chitterlings are pig's intestines cooked as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig's small intestines prepared as food, so animal guts.
